title: Power, brightness, and heat
description: Power is how fast energy is spent. A bright lamp and a hot wire can spend the same energy in different ways.

blocks.md:
## P = V × I

Power is how fast energy is spent. A simple relation is P = V × I. A bright lamp spends energy as light (and some heat). A skinny wire with a huge current spends energy as heat. Same idea, different place.

This bites when you think “more current is always a better lamp.” Extra current in a short is extra heat in the easy wire, often while the lamp is skipped. Brightness is one use of power. Heat is another.

![Light and heat are both power](assets/power-heat.svg)

```text
P = V × I
same V, larger I  →  larger P  →  brighter or hotter
```

A common mistake is cheering for a short as “more power.” The questions ask you to compute a small P and to say where the energy goes.

blocks.promptMd: V = 2 and I = 1. What is P?
blocks.explainMd: P = 2 × 1 = 2. Power is the product, not a third kind of juice.

blocks.promptMd: A short around a lamp usually spends most of the extra power as…
blocks.explainMd: The easy path takes the current. That path gets hot. The lamp may even go dark.

blocks.promptMd: If voltage stays the same and current doubles, power doubles.
blocks.explainMd: P = V × I. Same V, double I, double P.
